failure_summary.description: Agents returned an associated proper noun, formula, holiday purpose, or truth judgment instead of the entity requested by the clue.
Answers used an unnecessarily expanded name, an exhaustive list, or the wrong grammatical number despite the expected concise form.

patch.reasoning: Most failures already have direct guidance in the skill and appear to reflect ignored target-selection or minimality rules, so duplicating those rules is unwarranted. The name-form guidance does contain a tension: it encourages retaining conventional initials even when a shorter, unambiguous form is directly supported. Tightening that tie-break addresses the repeated over-expanded-name errors.

edits.target: When choosing a name form, distinguish identity-bearing parts from generic type words supplied by the clue. Retain conventional initials that belong to a person's identifying name; omit a generic label such as an entity type or location type when the clue supplies that type and the shorter name identifies the answer unambiguously.
edits.content: When choosing a name form, distinguish identity-bearing parts from generic type words supplied by the clue. Include conventional initials when the clue uses them or they are needed to disambiguate; otherwise prefer the shorter conventional name form directly supported by the question or context. Omit a generic label such as an entity type or location type when the clue supplies that type and the shorter name identifies the answer unambiguously.
